newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FULL TEXT - Philippine Central Bank statement.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT - Philippine Central Bank statement.

text.p: The following is the statement by Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson on the peso on Friday:

"Starting today, July 11, 1997, the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) (Central Bank) will allow the peso-U.S. dollar rate to move within a new wider range consistent with significantly changed market conditions. This is expected to remove the incentive for speculation against the peso and allow a gradual reduction in interest rates more compatible with the economy's requirements for sustainable economic growth."

"The BSP remains fully committed to the market-oriented exchange rate arrangement which has served the Philippines well. While the underlying exchange rate policy will remain unchanged, the BSP will allow greater flexibility in the peso-U.S. dollar rate. This is being taken to facilitate more timely adjustment in light of more difficult conditions in regional currency markets.
"The move towards greater exchange rate flexibility will be done in the context of sustained prudence in macroeconomic policies.
"Monetary policy will remain consistent with low and stable inflation while accommodating the requirements of sustainable economic growth.

"The Government will also continue its firm fiscal policy mainly by intensifying its efforts to boost revenues. These measures, together with authorities' efforts to seek a successful tax reform, reaffirm the Government's commitment to sound financial policies."
